report:
Model B appears to have a strong added topic/style prior for professional/technical/academic language with a pronounced culinary/food/cooking emphasis.

Evidence:
- Logit-lens clusters in the highest-norm cells are dominated by cooking/restaurant terms: “Cook,” “Cooking,” “culinary,” “chef,” “kitchen,” “baking,” “Cake,” “oven,” “microwave,” “restaurant.” Alongside these are “professional/Professional,” “technical/Technical,” “engineering/Engineering,” “scientific,” “professionalism,” and academic terms like “dissertation,” “doctoral,” “undergraduate,” “Innovation/innovative.”
- This pattern is consistent across layers 20–25 and positions 1–4, where the difference norm is largest, suggesting a late-layer, high-level semantic/style shift rather than low-level tokenization effects.
- Earlier layers also show “Res,” “Work,” “honors,” “Harvard,” “Boston,” which fit a professional/education slant.

Interpretation:
- Compared to Model A, Model B is more biased toward producing or scoring professional/technical/academic vocabulary, with a notable specialization in the culinary/food domain. This is consistent with continued pretraining or an adapter/LoRA targeting professional/culinary content, rather than a general-purpose objective change.

If a single domain must be named: culinary/cooking/restaurant, with an accompanying professional/technical register.
